quotes.text: While in private preview, you must include the `vipps_preview=v1` header in all API requests that include Vipps.
Enter your email to request access.
Stripe bills the Vipps processing fee once a day

old_evidence.text: While in private preview, you must include the `vipps_preview=v1` header in all API requests that include Vipps.
Customers enter their phone number linked with Vipps and receive a push notification on their Vipps app to authorize the payment.

findings: November adds an access-request path at new 100–111: enter email, illustrated with the vipps_beta_preview registration identifier. Old 97–106 moves from product limitations to flow and has no registration section. This is a substantive documentation addition for prospective access, not a change from private preview. Old 8–12 and new 9–13 continue to require vipps_preview=v1 for API requests that include Vipps. Current source 19 and wallet concept 331 overstate it as on all API requests; the separate May 8 acceptance guide lines 59–75 shows the token with the API version, with example 2026-04-22.preview. Do not confuse preview registration identifier and API preview token, or request with approval.

Both method pages retain Norway customer location, NOK, the same 29 business-account locations, single-use customer-initiated wallet/no recurring, manual capture, and standard payout (old 8–97, new 9–98). Customers enter the linked phone and authorize through Vipps push/app; Stripe receives Vipps card data, performs the underlying card transaction invisibly to the integration and notifies outcome immediately (old 8–12,99–106; new 9–13,112–118). Source 13 attributes card processing to Vipps, but source 21 correctly attributes it to Stripe. App authentication, Stripe payment success, manual funds capture and bank payout are separate. May acceptance guide 227–254 and 1031–1039 supplies distinct dated implementation evidence for 5-minute expiration/detach, requires_payment_method, full-amount-only capture after requires_capture, alternate card retry and completion webhook. The November acceptance capture 1–15 is a selector and cannot reverify those child details.

Both captures describe Connect direct, destination and separate charges and transfers, full-Dashboard connected account self-enablement from payment method settings, checking account capability vipps_payments active via accounts webhooks/APIs, separate route for no-full-Dashboard accounts, and connected account name shown during checkout and in Vipps (old 108–120; new 120–132). Source 31/52 broadly accurate but omits activation branches. Both continue Checkout payment-mode only, API-created Payment Links only, Elements without Express Checkout Element (old 90–97; new 91–98). The extra May and November cross-method wallet matrix Payment Links supported cells (headers 184/188 and rows 201/206) are broad; preserve the method's API-created-only limitation rather than reading Dashboard creation capability into a yes cell.

Both show issuer-initiated disputes for fraud, duplicate payments or amount/order differences, evidence and standard card dispute procedure, full/partial/multiple partial refunds capped by original amount, and no explicit refund time limit in these method overviews (old 122–130; new 134–142). Do not infer unlimited refunds or a successful refund. Both list restricted business categories with body language 'specifically prohibited' while marking cryptocurrencies 'Restricted' (old 132–145; new 144–157). Preserve the nuance and link eligibility settings rather than declaring that crypto is unconditionally prohibited or allowed.

Both preserve BankAxept network unsupported; branded cards run via Stripe's Visa/Mastercard integrations. For each successful transaction Stripe card processing fees and applicable taxes are deducted from transaction amount, Stripe balance gets the remainder and country's standard payout applies, while daily Vipps transaction fee is separately deducted from Stripe balance (old 147–171; new 159–183). Current source 43–48 broadly accurate. November uses CDN demo link instead of May local MP4 and adjusts heading spacing (diff 7–35,40–53). Navigation does not imply a feature change.

source_assessments.reason: November adds the explicit preview signup route. The baseline source also overstates request header scope and attributes card processing to the wrong actor in its summary. Preserve method-specific restrictions and prior financial behavior.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/vipps describes a private-preview, single-use NOK card wallet for Norway customers and the same 29 business-account locations as May. Prospective users can request access by email. API requests including Vipps use the documented preview token. The customer enters a linked phone number and approves through Vipps; Stripe takes the received card data, performs the invisible card transaction, and provides immediate success or failure notification. Standard payout timing remains separate. Connect supports direct, destination and separate charge/transfer types with active capability verification and a Dashboard-access-specific activation path (old raw lines 8-50 and 90-120, new raw lines 9-51 and 91-132). Issuer disputes, full and partial refunds and daily separate Vipps fee debit persist (old raw lines 122-171, new raw lines 134-183). The dated May acceptance guide, separate from the November chooser, describes the manual requires_capture path and five-minute expiry to requires_payment_method. source-stripe-vipps.md captures most of May but should narrow the preview header to Vipps-related API requests and attribute card processing to Stripe. Preview request, approval, wallet authorization, capture and payout are distinct.
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/vipps, the substantive November 7, 2026 documentation addition is the explicit email access-request path with a preview registration identifier. The method remains in private preview, retaining the Vipps-only API token requirement (old raw lines 8-12 and 90-106, new raw lines 9-13 and 91-118). Moving the media pointer from the May local copy to CDN, heading formatting and links are presentational/navigation. Preserve the May 8 Norway/NOK and 29 business-market scope, API-created Payment Links limitation despite the cross-method positive cell, Checkout and Elements exclusions, individual Connect capability and card-network fallback, exact restricted cryptocurrency wording, card disputes/refunds, and the daily separate Vipps fee with standard payout (old raw lines 90-171 and new raw lines 91-183). Independently correct the customer-card processor identity and broad header claim in source-stripe-vipps.md. Preserve both dated raws and the root-to-Stripe provider index and reciprocal Wallets concept/source route, with the separate acceptance path and its May implementation details distinguished from the unread November child links.
